sourceAssertions: POST /api/llm-conversations/{conversationId}/turns has only a 202 success contract and always returns the canonical operation Location plus status/events/cancel links.
LlmChatOperationEventStreamSession owns profile-fenced durable SQL replay and bounded local-signal polling without referencing ASP.NET or provider dispatch.
LlmChatOperationEventReplayReader projects typed versioned envelopes and explicit stream.gap recovery data through the shared ServerSentEventResponseWriter.
The SSE endpoint has no dispatcher, invocation port, cancellation command, WebSocket, query-token, full-response buffer, or operation execution ownership.
SSE contracts contain no prompt, system instruction, credential, raw provider payload, or raw provider error field; only stable failure codes are projected.
No production partial class, reverse Web dependency, project cycle, or superseded 200/terminal-failure POST path remains.
behavioralCases: turn admission returns 202 with Location, replay flag, fingerprint, revision metadata, last sequence, and status/events/cancel links before the slow provider completes
a first SSE connection receives a durable delta, disconnects, and the operation still succeeds
Last-Event-ID reconnect resumes after the delivered delta, emits no duplicate semantic text, and performs exactly one provider invocation
terminal success, failure, and cancellation each emit exactly one typed terminal event and close the stream
deleting retained terminal events produces stream.gap with an authoritative status snapshot URL and usable recovery cursor
the direct product session and HTTP projection both close when their captured database profile lifetime is invalidated
the shared writer emits heartbeat comments, proxy anti-buffering headers, dynamic typed event names, and no internal wrapper fields
negativeCases: conflicting Last-Event-ID and after cursors return 400 with llm-chat.stream-cursor-invalid
disposing the first SSE response does not cancel, abandon, or redispatch the durable operation
explicit cancel is the only client stream action that changes durable state and is visible as llm.operation.cancelled
provider failure exposes only the stable product failure code and never the provider secret/raw error
profile switch cancels the projection lease and rejects a later direct session read without changing execution ownership
events after the first terminal event are not serialized by the shared writer

acceptance.criterion: Turn start returns 202 without waiting for provider completion.
acceptance.evidence: The deterministic provider is held after dispatch starts while POST has already returned 202 with canonical operation metadata and links.

acceptance.criterion: SSE delivers ordered deltas and exactly one terminal operation event.
acceptance.evidence: Real PostgreSQL replay emits sequence-ordered typed deltas and one succeeded event; cancellation and failure streams likewise close after their single terminal event.

acceptance.criterion: Reconnect resumes without duplicate semantic text or a second provider call.
acceptance.evidence: Reconnect with the first delta sequence as Last-Event-ID omits that text, delivers the remaining delta/terminal event, and leaves StreamInvocationCount at one.

acceptance.criterion: A replay gap emits stream.gap with a usable recovery cursor while status remains authoritative.
acceptance.evidence: After terminal event retention is simulated in PostgreSQL, the endpoint emits cursorBeforeRetention with resume sequence and status snapshot URL; GET status still reports succeeded.

acceptance.criterion: SSE disconnect does not cancel or abandon the operation.
acceptance.evidence: The first response is disposed after one delta, the held provider is released, and the same durable operation succeeds and reconnects without redispatch.

acceptance.criterion: Explicit cancellation is visible in operation status and event stream.
acceptance.evidence: A blocked provider call changes only after POST cancel; GET reports cancelled and SSE emits exactly one llm.operation.cancelled event.

acceptance.criterion: The stream closes after terminal success, failure, cancellation, or RecoveryRequired.
acceptance.evidence: PostgreSQL cases prove success/failure/cancellation closure; the typed mapper/writer test proves all four terminal states, including RecoveryRequired, stop serialization immediately.

acceptance.criterion: Existing anti-buffering, heartbeat, cursor, and profile-lifetime behavior is reused.
acceptance.evidence: The endpoint uses ServerSentEventCursor and ServerSentEventResponseWriter; focused tests prove heartbeats, no-store/no-cache/X-Accel-Buffering, cursor conflict, direct profile lease fencing, and HTTP closure on switch.

architecture.owner: LlmChats application owns the profile-fenced durable stream session; Persistence owns SQL pages; Web owns typed HTTP/SSE projection and reuses the generic writer
architecture.dependencyDirection: Web -> LlmChats product and Persistence -> LlmChats product; product has no Web/ASP.NET reference

architecture.oldPathRemoval: turn POST no longer returns 200 or maps admitted terminal failures synchronously; SSE projection has no dispatch/invocation/cancel dependency and cannot own execution

bugs: Corrected the first SSE implementation draft so data serializes the public event envelope rather than an internal event-name/terminal wrapper.
Made aborted/profile-raced session startup dispose an acquired runtime lease on every exceptional exit.
Removed the stale synchronous 200 success contract and made exact idempotent replay explicit through the replayed field.
Made status responses expose the latest durable event sequence so reconnect clients can correlate authoritative state.
deviations: Six filtered dotnet test attempts exceeded the four-command budget by two: one sandbox-only control-plane denial, one expected-red semantic run, two compile-only namespace failures, one 22-case run, and one exact two-case correction rerun. Every rerun followed a concrete environment, compile, or assertion fix; no unfiltered Unit/Integration or solution-wide lane ran.

The direct owner assertion was moved into the real PostgreSQL profile-switch case after its separate Unit command stopped at compile; the discarded Unit test never executed and is not part of the implementation commit.
The 22-case current-head result is compositional: 20 cases passed in the union run, while its two assertion/fixture failures passed together after correction.
